title: Evaluating and Improving Natural Language Autoencoders
abstract: arXiv:2611.19507v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Natural language autoencoders (NLAs) are a method for generating natural language explanations of LLM activations. We develop evaluations based on auditing tasks that test the ability of NLAs to surface latent knowledge, identify whether a model was misled by a hint, and catch a silent fabrication. We also develop extensions to NLAs that let them use activation information from multiple layers and positions, let us apply them more effectively to long transcripts, and reduce the number of false claims they make. These extensions result in improvements on both our auditing evaluations and auxiliary evaluations adapted from prior work. We also use the evaluations to study how different auditing capabilities change over the course of NLA training, and find that although every evaluation improves early in training, extended training can hurt performance on some of our auditing evaluations.

translated_title: 评估与改进自然语言自编码器
translated_abstract: 自然语言自编码器（NLAs）是一种为大语言模型（LLM）激活生成自然语言解释的方法。我们基于审计任务开发了一系列评估方法，用以测试自然语言自编码器揭示潜在知识、识别模型是否被提示误导以及捕捉无声捏造（silent fabrication）的能力。我们还开发了自然语言自编码器的扩展方法，使其能够利用来自多个层和位置的激活信息，从而更有效地应用于长篇对话记录，并减少其做出的虚假声明数量。这些扩展在我们的审计评估以及改编自先前工作的辅助评估上都带来了性能提升。我们还利用这些评估研究了不同的审计能力在自然语言自编码器训练过程中的变化，发现尽管每项评估在训练初期都有所改善，但过度训练可能会损害其在某些审计评估上的表现。
tldr: 提出基于审计任务的自然语言自编码器评估方法，并通过支持多层多位置激活信息利用、更适用于长文本和减少虚假声明等扩展改进，显著提升了自然语言自编码器解释大语言模型激活的能力。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces auditing-task-based evaluations for natural language autoencoders and proposes extensions—leveraging activations from multiple layers and positions, handling long transcripts, and reducing false claims—that consistently improve performance across both new and prior benchmarks.
